run.procedureSummary: 1 Feed: add the cycle's table amount to every chamber, LARVAL and PUPAL alike, with no holding-limit check. 2 Overflow: go through chambers 1 to 6 in order. Any mass over the holding limit moves into the next chamber, which leaves the chamber exactly at its limit. Because it runs in order, overflow cascades. Excess from chamber 6 goes onto the loss tally. This applies whatever the chamber's state. 3 Marks: use the mass after overflow. LARVAL at or above the upper mark becomes PUPAL. PUPAL at or below the lower mark becomes LARVAL. Otherwise nothing changes, and a chamber changes at most once per cycle. 4 Burn-off: compute all six amounts from the contents after marks, using the states after marks. LARVAL loses floor(mass/4) to the loss tally. PUPAL loses floor(mass/2) into chamber i-1 (toward 1), and chamber 1's PUPAL amount goes to the loss tally. All six are applied together, with no holding-limit check. 5 Moult: total the line after burn-off. If the total is strictly over 38, every chamber becomes floor(mass/2) and the removed mass (mass - floor(mass/2)) goes to the loss tally. At 38 or under, nothing happens. Five cycles are run in this order.

openPoints.assumption: The state after step 3 marks of the same cycle.
Overflow applies to every chamber regardless of state, and incoming overflow can push the receiving chamber over its own limit (cascade).

openPoints.point: Where PUPAL reabsorption goes, and how it is calculated
openPoints.assumption: It goes to the previous chamber (i-1, toward chamber 1). Amounts are computed from the contents before burn-off and applied at the same time, so a chamber can lose its own amount and receive one from chamber i+1 in the same step.
The new mass is floor(mass/2), and the remainder mass - floor(mass/2) (the larger half for odd masses) goes onto the loss tally.
No moult, because the rule says strictly over 38. In cycle 5 the total was exactly 38, so nothing happened.

openPoints.point: End masses above the holding limit
openPoints.assumption: They are left as they are after cycle 5 (chamber 2 = 10 > 8, chamber 4 = 7 > 6), as the write-up says excess waits and stays after cycle 5.
Both are inclusive: at or above the upper mark, at or below the lower mark.
